name: interaction_gap_20261110
status: exploratory CPU analysis; frozen before any target-level or model-level outcome was computed
question: Does same-pair information in other cell lines help through a pair-wide offset, a transferable cell-specific profile, or artifacts of reference construction and shared measurement?
seen_before_freeze: Monotherapy edges are identical across the replicate blocks of every pair-cell (182,316 groups) and across pairs sharing a drug, cell line and dose (pooled SD 0.0006).
315 pair-cells (21 pairs x 15 cell lines) carry a second set of four blocks deposited later (source_row >= 2273700); 75 of them (5 pairs) use different dose grids.
Raw pair-cell mean inhibition of the two sets differs far more than within-set replicate dispersion predicts (all 315, unprojected, dose-confounded pairs included).
No contrast target, variance component, anchor-model or control outcome had been computed.
unit: pair-cell: one drug pair x one cell line; all combination rows of its blocks

targets.T_bliss: primary. Row-weighted pair-cell mean of (unit mean inhibition - frozen Bliss reference), residualized on additive endpoint-drug indicators within (original pair fold, cell line) with row-count weights. Identical to the frozen pair_cell:bliss_residual estimand.
targets.T_raw: same contrast applied to unit mean inhibition (measured combination response, reference-free).
targets.T_ref: same contrast applied to the frozen Bliss reference (reference-only control); T_raw = T_ref + T_bliss.
targets.T_train: pair-cell mean Bliss residual minus an additive drug-by-cell baseline (row-weighted least squares on drug indicators, per cell line) fitted only on pairs outside the excluded folds.

noise.split: block signs balanced within (pair-cell, dose-grid group), as frozen
noise.batch_split: block signs balanced within (pair-cell, batch, dose-grid group)

cross_batch.eligible: 8-block pair-cells whose two dose grids agree within |log ratio| <= 0.02 at every rank
cross_batch.targets: each batch alone substitutes the pair-cell mean (weight 64) in the frozen panel contrast; references from block edges
adjustments: batch-2 minus batch-1 mean shift per cell line removed before the contrast

variance_components.pair_wide: row-weighted cross-cell U-statistic sum_p sum_{c!=c'} w t w' t' / sum_p sum_{c!=c'} w w'
variance_components.out_of_sample: leave-one-cell-out B1 and B2 with covariance estimated on the other folds

negative_controls.pair_permutation: pair labels permuted within each (fold, cell) panel independently per cell; 20 permutations, seed 17
negative_controls.zero_interaction: rows replaced by the frozen Bliss reference plus block-sign-flipped centred replicate deviations scaled by sqrt(n/(n-1)); 5 realizations, seed 19
negative_controls.reference_perturbation: shared monotherapy values perturbed by independent N(0, s^2) per (drug, cell, dose), s in {2, 5, 10}; 10 draws, seed 23; Bliss recomputed from block-edge monotherapy
negative_controls.hsa_convention: contrast of (truth - max(a, b)) from block edges

anchor_experiment.folds: original five pair folds; test fold f, validation fold (f+1) mod 5
anchor_experiment.mask: per (pair_id, seed): numpy default_rng(int(sha256('pair_id|seed')[:16], 16)).permutation of the pair's sorted cell lines; anchors are the first k, evaluation cells are positions 16..end (identical for every k and model); masks never read targets

models.B0: zero (no same-pair information); for T_train the train-only baseline
models.B1: empirical-Bayes pair intercept: k tau2 / (s2 + k tau2) x mean of anchors; tau2 = cross-cell U-statistic, s2 = mean square - tau2, both on the four non-test folds
models.B2: best linear predictor from anchors with signal covariance K = lambda K_cs + (1 - lambda) (rank-r eigen part of the noise-corrected cross-cell covariance + residual diagonal), observation noise per cell added on anchors; lambda in {0, .25, .5, .75, 1}, r in {1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 20, 38}; selected per (target, fold, k) on validation pairs with covariance from the remaining three folds, then refit on the four non-test folds
models.B3: saved pair-seen F2 predictions, projected contrast, only in the matched pair-cell-split condition
models.B4: B1 and B2 fed the anchors of a donor pair sharing exactly one drug (non-test folds, chosen by hash of pair_id, seed)
models.B5a: B1 and B2 fed the anchors of a donor pair sharing no drug
models.B5b: B2 fed the pair's own anchor values on deranged anchor cells (k >= 2)

anchor_experiment.loco: B1 and B2 with all other cells as anchors (out-of-sample predictable shares)
anchor_experiment.matched_b3: pair-cell split: anchors are the pair's cells in folds not in {f, f+1}; B2 selected on fold f+1; evaluated on fold f with and without the panel projection of out-of-fold predictions
anchor_experiment.metrics: row-weighted SSE, MSE (per row weight), RMSE, R2 = 1 - SSE/SSE(B0) on identical rows, pair-macro R2 (mean and median), noise share of evaluated rows reported separately
anchor_experiment.materiality: a difference is material if >= 0.01 R2 and both the pair-bootstrap and drug-jackknife 95% intervals exclude zero; B1 explains almost all of the pair-seen gain if matched R2(B1) >= 0.9 R2(B3); transferable cell structure is substantial if B2 - B1 >= 0.02 at k = 16 and at LOCO

experiment_c: residual after the anchor-derived B1 intercept on evaluation cells: B2 versus B1 residual R2, replicate noise of the residual from the split draws, cross-batch reproducibility of the pair-centred residual
